why: Level flag only. A state verb about this moment (not *am knowing*) is a B1.1 point of the present_simple card; the new built-in replacement is fine, one answer, wrong options are real mistakes (3S, continuous of a state verb).

Readers: the forms are not named. That is the rule (3 November: give the situation, the check looks for the form). r21b-1-019 already aligned the checks: going to / about to for the evidence ('what we can see now: Look at the clouds! It's going to rain' on the future card), I'll / Shall I for the offer; 'might' is not on the card and is rejected.

Tested the checks: natural answers pass (Could you tell me / Do you know / I'd like to know / I wonder / Would you mind telling me + question word or if + statement order); 'when is the', 'when does the', 'if did you', 'when starts the' fail. But 'Could you possibly tell me', 'Would you be able to tell me', 'Can I ask …' and 'Do you have any idea …' (correct polite starts a learner writes) failed checks 1 and 2; both now take them. Readers' 'form not named' / 'a direct question is polite too' is the rule (3 and 21 November: give the situation, the check looks for the form), as r21b-1-038 decided.

must: \b(could|can|would) you (please |possibly |kindly |just )?(tell me|let me know|check|find out|confirm)\b|\bwould you be able to (tell me|let me know|check|find out|confirm)\b|\bwould you mind (telling me|checking)\b|\bdo you (happen to )?know\b|\b(do you have|have you got|have you) any idea\b|\b(can|could|may) i ask\b|\bi[\'’]?d like to (know|ask)\b|\bi would like to (know|ask)\b|\bi (was )?wonder(ing)?\b
Start politely: *Could you tell me …?*, *Do you know …?* or *I'd like to know …*
Sāc pieklājīgi: *Could you tell me …?*, *Do you know …?* vai *I'd like to know …*
\b(tell me|let me know|check|find out|confirm|telling me|checking|know|wonder|wondering|ask|idea),?\s+(please,?\s+)?((on|at|in|from) )?(if|whether|when|what|where|why|how|who|which)\b
Then a question word or *if*: *… when the next course starts*.
Tad jautājamais vārds vai *if*: *… when the next course starts*.

^(?!.*\b(if|whether|when|where|why|who|how(?:\s+(?:long|soon|much|many|often|far)(?:\s+\w+)?)?|what(?:\s+\w+)?|which(?:\s+\w+)?)\s+(?:(?:do|does|did|is|are|was|were|has|have|had|could|would|should)(?:n[\'’]t)?|will|won[\'’]t|can|can[\'’]t|cannot)\s+(you|he|she|it|they|we|i|the|my|your|our|his|her|their|this|that|these|those|someone|somebody|anyone|anybody|there|mine)\b)
After the question word the subject comes first, with no *do / does*: *when the course starts*, not *when does the course start*.
Pēc jautājamā vārda sākumā ir teikuma priekšmets, bez *do / does*: *when the course starts*, nevis *when does the course start*.
^(?!.*\b(?:when|where|why|what time|what day|what date|how much|how long|how soon|how often)\s+(?!(?:is|was|has|does)\b)\w+s\s+(?:the|my|your|our|his|her|their|this|that)\b)
Put the subject before the verb: *when the course starts*, not *when starts the course*.
Teikuma priekšmets ir pirms darbības vārda: *when the course starts*, nevis *when starts the course*.
